translations.text: But the ungodly summoned death to themselves by their deeds and words. They regarded it as a friend and wasted away, and they made a covenant with it, for they are indeed worthy to share in it.
Let our strength be the law of righteousness, for weakness proves to be useless.
Let us see whether his words are true, and let us put his end to the test.
For whoever despises wisdom and instruction is miserable. Their hope is empty, their labors are fruitless, and their deeds are useless.
Their wives are foolish, and their children are wicked.
For even if it buds with branches for a time, its frail [?] will be shaken by the wind and uprooted by the force of the wind.
For God's judgment is upon his holy ones, and his visitation is upon his chosen ones.
All that passed like a shadow and like the report of a man running past.
Therefore, be instructed by my words and benefit from them.
For he gave me unerring knowledge of things that exist, to know the structure of the world and the workings of the elements.
God loves no one except the one who lives with wisdom.
So I resolved to take her as my companion for life, knowing that she would counsel me in good things and comfort me in cares and sorrow.
Then the paths of those on earth were made straight, people learned your ways, and they were saved by your wisdom.

She guided the righteous man along straight paths when he fled from his brother's anger. She showed him the kingdom of God and gave him knowledge of holy things. She prospered him with gains from his labors and multiplied the fruit of his work.
Therefore the righteous plundered the ungodly and blessed your holy name, Lord, and together they praised your hand, which fought on their behalf.
You were not powerless in battle to deliver the ungodly into the hands of the righteous, or to crush them with fearsome beasts, or all at once, in an instant, with a word.

For who will say to you, 'What have you done?' Or who will oppose your judgment? Who will reproach you for the destruction of nations that you created? Or who will come against you to avenge unrighteous people?
Instead, they regarded as gods either fire, wind, swift air, the courses of the stars, the powerful waters, or the heavenly lights that govern the world.
For from the greatness and beauty of created things, their maker can also be seen by comparison.
Or he fashioned it in the likeness of a worthless animal. He coated it with [?], reddened its color with vermilion, and plastered all its [?] with clay.

For he vainly fashions a god from the same clay—he who was himself formed from the earth a little while ago, and after a short time returns to the place from which he was taken, when the debt of his soul is demanded.
For they were stung again to remind them of your words, and were quickly rescued, so that they would not fall into deep forgetfulness and be left without the protection of your kindness.
For neither medicines nor poultices healed them, but your word, Lord, which heals everything.
For you have authority over life and death; you bring down to the realm of the dead and bring up again.
But a human being kills through his own wickedness, and the departed spirit does not return, nor is the breath that has been taken captive released.
And the new and marvelous thing was that fire worked even more powerfully in water, which extinguishes everything, for the world fights on behalf of the righteous.
For your judgments are great and hard to explain; therefore, souls without instruction went astray.
For some did not welcome the strangers who came, while the others enslaved guests who had benefited them.

For on their account the elements were harmonized as on a harp: each, with its own tuned sounds, sounded its own name, always remaining in the same tone. This can truly be inferred from the sight of what happened.
Fire overcame water by its own power, and water forgot its own extinguishing nature.
